sections.h2: Ways to sell a house fast in Longview
sections.html:
You can sell in Longview through an agent, on your own, or to a cash buyer who accepts the house in its present state. Three factors choose for you: your closing deadline, the repairs needed, and the amount of price you will exchange for speed.

Before comparing routes, pull four items together.

  • Your parcel number and newest tax statement from the Cowlitz County Treasurer.
  • Payoff figures from every lender or lienholder.
  • Notes on repairs, additions and remodels, with permit numbers if you have them.
  • The finished seller disclosure statement Washington asks for in most home sales.

A listing tends to attract the most buyers and the best price, and it brings showings, inspections and a wait on the buyer's loan. Cash avoids nearly all of that, and the price is where you pay for it.

Roughly 38,000 people live in Longview, and owners hold just over half of the homes, which leaves a large rental share. When a tenant occupies your house, read the lease before you commit to a closing date. The median home value comes from a survey of owner-occupied homes, so order a real valuation for yours.

sections.h2: Older homes and the outside of the house
sections.html:
A lumber company drew up Longview on paper before building it, and the Civic Center is a National Register historic district. Buildings from the 1923 to 1934 boom years lean Georgian-revival, Tudor and craftsman. A house from that period can charm buyers who want character, yet an inspector may flag aging wiring, plumbing or foundation. Western valley subdivisions arrived later, in the 1960s.

Wet, windy, overcast weather means roofs, gutters and drainage get close scrutiny from buyers and inspectors. Walk the exterior before you list or accept an offer.

  • Look at roof surfaces and flashing for pieces lifted or missing after windy spells.
  • Clear the gutters and make sure downspouts send water away from the foundation.
  • Check crawl spaces and low walls for damp spots.
  • Cut back branches hanging over the roof or the power line.

Handle these first and buyers have fewer reasons to ask for credits.

The city's Community Development office is your first stop. It issues building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits and handles zoning and code compliance. Find it at 1525 Broadway Street in Longview City Hall, where hours are 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Thursday, with Fridays closed. Call 360-442-5086 or write permits@ci.longview.wa.us. Archived and recent property records are searchable online too.

Three questions are worth answering there before you sell.

  • Did you or a past owner obtain permits for an addition, finished basement, new deck or re-roof?
  • Does any code compliance case remain open on the property?
  • Does zoning permit what the layout now shows, such as an accessory dwelling or a second kitchen?

Unpermitted work does not make a sale impossible, but it often becomes a repair credit, a lower price or a question from the buyer's lender. Cash buyers commonly accept the work as it is and lower the offer. In every case, describe the work honestly on the disclosure.

sections.h2: What Washington law requires from a Longview seller
sections.html:
For most sales of improved residential property, Washington requires the seller to hand over a completed disclosure statement and places the real estate excise tax on the seller. RCW 64.06.020 gives you five business days from the buyer's and seller's acceptance of a written contract to deliver the statement, unless you both agree to another timeline in writing. The buyer may then rescind within three business days.

Excise tax has a state share and a local add-on, and the county treasurer where the property is located collects it on the sale date. RCW 82.45.060 sets the state share in four bands. Beginning January 1, 2027, the lowest band covers the first $551,000 at a rate of 1.1 percent. The next covers up to $1,551,000 at 1.28 percent, then up to $3,051,000 at 2.75 percent, with 3 percent charged on anything higher.

A closing before 2027 uses the earlier breakpoints of $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. The Cowlitz County Treasurer can tell you the local rate for your address and the combined amount at your price. With a median home value near $361,600, most Longview sales land in the lowest band.

sections.h2: Cowlitz County property taxes at sale time
sections.html:
Bills go out from Cowlitz County each February, with payments due April 30 and October 31. Mail yours to the Treasurer at 207 N 4th Ave in Kelso with a postmark on or before the deadline, since a late payment adds interest and penalties. A mid-period closing means title or escrow divides the bill between you and the buyer, and your settlement statement should show a proration line.

To challenge the assessed value, phone the Assessor at 360-577-3010 and speak with an appraiser. That call alone does not protect an appeal. You also need a petition filed with the Board of Equalization, 207 4th Avenue N in Kelso, and the county's deadline is July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the value notice went out, whichever comes later.

sections.h2: Weighing a cash offer against a listing
sections.html:
Rate each route by the money you actually keep, never the advertised figure. Commissions, excise tax, buyer repair requests and months of carrying an unsold house all shrink a listing price. A cash offer usually starts lower but can eliminate several of those costs and shorten the schedule.

Put identical questions to every buyer. What is the exact price? Which closing date can they commit to? Who covers excise tax and title costs? Does the offer hinge on an inspection or on financing? Before you sign, let a title company or attorney read the purchase agreement.

Interstate 5 passes through the corridor. State Routes 4 and 432 lead to Kelso and Wahkiakum County, and the Lewis and Clark Bridge on State Route 433 crosses the Columbia into Rainier, Oregon. Buses from RiverCities Transit connect Longview and Kelso. The city stands where the Cowlitz and Columbia rivers meet and borders Kelso, the county seat.

Buyers with children ask about schools early. Longview Public Schools operates eight elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools.

faqs.q: Do I have to make repairs before selling my Longview house?
faqs.a: No, Washington does not require repairs before a sale. You must still complete the seller disclosure statement honestly, and a buyer who sees defects may ask for a lower price or credits. A cash sale as-is skips the repair work but usually lowers the offer.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax in a Longview sale?
faqs.a: Typically the seller. If the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible. It goes to the Cowlitz County Treasurer on the sale date, so include it when you estimate proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Cowlitz County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31. The county mails bills each February, and a mailed check postmarked by the due date is on time. Later payments add interest and penalties.

faqs.q: How long does the seller disclosure take in Washington?
faqs.a: You have five business days after both sides accept a written contract, unless you agree to another time in writing. The buyer then has three business days to rescind. RCW 64.06.020 contains the form and the timing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Longview house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but disclose it. Call the city's Community Development office at 360-442-5086 to learn which permits are on file. A buyer using a loan may ask for the work to be permitted or priced in, while a cash buyer may accept it as is and trim the offer.
